title: Repeated quantity heads distinguish local pairing from one coordinated amount scope
summary: GDT759 records adjacent amount heads in exact expressions, including ar al ar aiin. A narrow exploratory question is whether each quantity head pairs locally with its following value/part, or whether the first head scopes over a coordinated multi-item amount expression.

design.mechanism: local quantity-scope pairing versus one coordinated multi-item amount scope
design.unit: reader-exact multi-head amount span with independently segmented value/part candidates
design.contrast: each amount head locally binds its following value/part versus the first amount head governs the full coordinated span
design.prediction: In held multi-head spans, local pairing predicts stable head-to-following-value alignment and independent alternation of the second head; a single-scope analysis predicts the first head remains sufficient when the later value changes.
design.countermodel: Repeated heads may be template padding or duplicated notation for one amount, so apparent local pairing can arise without two semantic scopes.
design.falsifier: After preregistering segmentation and independent value/part coding, held multi-head spans show no stable local pairing and are equally explained by one first-head scope.
design.principal_risk: The source's working amount readings are not independent semantic gold; this cannot distinguish meanings unless value/part coding is independently bound.
design.related: Near IDEA000014 (one measured entity), IDEA000032 (generic coordination), GDT759 and GDT760, but targets the falsifiable scope relation inside exact multi-head spans rather than amount conservation or side attachment.

source_evidence.quote:
## Die drei Mengenköpfe unterscheiden sich

| Kopf | exakte Wertpaare | beobachtete Werte | Arbeitsfunktion |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `s` | 25 | II, III, IV | Drachmen-/Maßformel; gleich-Teile-Rivale |
| `or` | 44 | II, III, IV | Portionen |
| `ar` | 27 | II, III, IV | Anteile |

Die konkreten Hauptausdrücke sind `or aiin=drei Portionen` (36-mal) und
`ar aiin=drei Anteile` (16-mal). Neben den vier `s aiin/saiin`-Brücken gibt
es je eine vollständig normalisierte Brücke für `or ain/orain`,
`or aiin/oraiin` und `ar aiin/araiin`. Leerzeichen trennen hier also nicht
zuverlässig Wort von Kompositum.

Beispielausschnitte:

```text
f16r.7   ... schy s aiin doal ...
          ... schy; drei Drachmen; doal ...

f76r.47  ... chckhy or aiin sheey ...
          ... chckhy; drei Portionen; sheey ...

f113v.2  ... ar al ar aiin okal ...
          ... Anteil; al; drei Anteile; okal ...
```

design.smallest_next_step: Check all exact multi-head spans for independently coded value/part boundaries; stop if those labels are inherited working defaults.
